questions.stem: Methane (CH4) has an energy content of 56 kJ/g, while octane (C8H18) has 48 kJ/g. A camping stove needs to boil water using the minimum mass of fuel. Which fuel is more efficient per gram?

options.text: Octane, because it has more carbon atoms to burn
Methane, because it releases more energy per gram
Both are equally efficient as they are both hydrocarbons
Octane, because larger molecules always release more energy

questions.explanation: Per gram, methane releases 56 kJ compared to octane's 48 kJ. This means less methane (by mass) is needed to boil the water. Methane has a higher proportion of hydrogen atoms relative to carbon, and C-H and H-O bonds contribute significantly to the overall energy released during combustion.

questions.stem: When a hydrocarbon fuel undergoes incomplete combustion instead of complete combustion, which of the following is true?

options.text: More energy is released because more products are formed
Less energy is released because not all carbon is fully oxidised to CO2
The same energy is released regardless of whether combustion is complete or incomplete
No energy is released during incomplete combustion

questions.explanation: In incomplete combustion, some carbon forms CO or soot (C) instead of CO2. Since C-O bonds in CO2 release energy when formed, making fewer CO2 molecules means less energy is released overall. Incomplete combustion also produces toxic carbon monoxide and wastes fuel, making it both less efficient and more dangerous.

questions.stem: Hydrogen is considered a clean fuel for vehicles. What is the only product when hydrogen burns in oxygen, and why is this considered 'clean'?

options.text: Carbon dioxide; it is clean because CO2 is a natural gas
Water; it produces no carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, or particulates
Helium; it is a noble gas and harmless
Oxygen; the reaction recycles oxygen back into the atmosphere

questions.explanation: The combustion of hydrogen produces only water: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O. This is considered clean because there are no carbon-containing products (no CO2 contributing to climate change, no CO which is toxic, no soot particles causing air pollution). However, challenges include hydrogen storage, production methods, and safety.

questions.stem: A student compares two fuels by burning 1 g of each under identical conditions to heat 100 g of water. Fuel A raises the temperature by 30°C and Fuel B by 22°C. Which fuel has a higher energy density (energy per gram)?

options.text: Fuel B, because it has a lower temperature rise
Both fuels have the same energy density
Fuel A, because it produces a greater temperature rise per gram
Cannot be determined without knowing the molecular formulae

questions.explanation: Using Q = mcDeltaT with equal mass of water and fuel: Fuel A releases Q = 100 x 4.2 x 30 = 12,600 J per gram, while Fuel B releases Q = 100 x 4.2 x 22 = 9,240 J per gram. Since both used 1 g of fuel, Fuel A has a higher energy density. The greater temperature rise directly indicates more energy released per gram.

questions.stem: Fossil fuels like coal, oil, and natural gas are described as non-renewable energy resources. What does 'non-renewable' mean in this context?

options.text: They cannot be used more than once
They are being used faster than they can be replaced by natural processes, so they will eventually run out
They produce pollution when burned
They are very expensive to extract from the ground

questions.explanation: Non-renewable means the resources are formed over millions of years (from ancient organisms) but are consumed much faster than they form. At current rates of use, they will eventually be depleted. This is different from renewable resources like biofuels or solar energy, which can be replenished within a human lifetime.
